prompt:
Documentary-editorial photograph for a world-class creative agency's own brand book: the craft itself, caught in the act, not a meeting. Medium-format look, impeccable craft, natural true-to-life color with NO color grading, no filter, no HDR. COLOR SYSTEM: a calm, tonal background field; skin and real materials; and exactly ONE vivid accent of bright active blue (#0375DB, a saturated azure blue) coming from light or a single object, never from walls. No navy walls. Highlights keep detail (never blown), shadows open with detail (never crushed), moderate contrast. CASTING: Latin American professionals with natural, characterful, non-model faces, varied ages, real working clothes, genuine attitude and gestures (focus, a small laugh, pointing, deciding); nobody looks at the camera. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks anywhere (screens and prints show only images and abstract shapes). Vertical 4:5.

SCENE: trade marketing in retail. A paint and home-improvement store aisle in Mexico City; a tall, well-lit shelf display of paint cans, most in neutral colors and one hero section of cans in bright active blue (#0375DB) with no readable labels; an Efeonce trade marketer (a Peruvian man in his thirties) checks the display on a tablet while the store manager (a Mexican woman in her fifties in a store apron) adjusts the front row of cans. 35mm lens at f/2.8, camera at cart-handle height, focus on the two people and the hero section.

FOREGROUND (planned, the product itself, shooting through the shelf): the camera sits at the level of the lowest shelf, so a row of plain matte graphite-grey paint cans (no labels) on the near shelf is very close to the lens and spans the ENTIRE width of the bottom 20% of the frame, falling out of focus GRADUALLY (smooth optical falloff, never a hard band), DARK graphite in soft shadow; its center area is calm and even (no highlights or details there).
